title: improv·artist · tender (Felix Gonzalez-Torres)
mutation_directive: improv artist: tender via Felix Gonzalez-Torres

improv_extras.practice: candy spills, light strings, paired clocks; intimacy as sculpture

v1.feedback: The Gonzalez-Torres light-string reference lands clearly — catenary droop, warm incandescent pulse, dark gallery void. The form reads in under 2 seconds as draped bulb strings, and the sway is gentle enough to feel tender rather than busy. To push further: lean into the 'paired' intimacy — two distinct clusters of strings (not 14 evenly spread) would echo his use of doubling (paired clocks, two candy piles); right now the strings read as a single installation wall rather than a dialogue between two bodies. Consider dimming outlier particles more aggressively so individual bulbs pop against the droop, closer to his actual warm-white-on-dark contrast.

v2.feedback: The paired-cluster catenary concept maps well to Gonzalez-Torres' light strings and the gap between them reads as intimacy, but the sim shader's restX restore math is broken (mod of signed offsets will scatter particles to wrong rest positions), so strings will drift and lose their draped form over time. The warm incandescent palette is restrained and appropriate. Drop the broken restX spring entirely — anchor each particle to its init position stored in a separate texture lookup instead, and add a faint connecting wire (GL_LINES or thin additive trail) between bulbs so the string reads as a string, not a dotted line of floating orbs. The vAlpha lineDist suppression based on a generic parabola is too aggressive and kills legitimate particles; tie it to per-particle init data instead.
